result.summary: The tenant says "the same problem as before" has come back, but doesn't say what the problem is. The CRM has no earlier maintenance case for this property in the last 24 months. I texted the tenant asking what the problem is, where it is, when it happened before and who fixed it, and asked for a photo. The same text gave emergency advice in case it turns out to be urgent. The ticket is on hold until tomorrow, when I'll chase the tenant if they haven't replied.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 001 doesn't describe any defect. Event 002 shows no earlier case to link it to, and the intake classifier couldn't categorise it (event 003). There's nothing to triage, cost or send to the landlord until the tenant says what the problem is, and they're the one person who can tell us quickly. The reply classifier marked the message 'review' (dissatisfied 0.93, safety concern 0.02). The safest useful step was a single clear request to the tenant, with emergency advice in case the problem is urgent.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The tenant can answer the missing details within a day. There's no safety signal and no complaint yet beyond mild frustration. If the tenant's reply points to an earlier repair arranged outside our records, or turns into a complaint, I'll escalate then.
There's no problem or cost to put to him yet. Contacting him now would only cause confusion.
The tenant is waiting, and the problem could be urgent.
